column1: # Every `.rs` the repository carries under `crates/` at or above 50 KiB, judged once.
# A size gate is a prohibitive gate: it names a shape that must not appear. Writing one
# without first counting the legitimate uses of that shape is how the first red turns out
# to be a file that was never supposed to be split. This table is that count.
#   multi-axis   the file carries two runtime entities that do not share a process, and
#                the `witness` column has to show it: the other side runs under its own
#                process entry point, a binary subcommand nothing else runs. That is the
#                axis the owner's 2026-10-14 ruling names, and it is the only one that
#                justifies a split by itself: the two sides are not co-present, so one
#                side's failure is invisible from the other, and a change to one is not a
#                change to the other. Two loops in one resident process are not this:
#                they are one subsystem, and splitting it buys no separation.
#   single-axis  one runtime entity, or one flow with several stages. Large is what its
#                job looks like, not a defect. Several of these are registries whose size
#                is the number of entries they hold; splitting one splits a single source
#   exempt       not production code, so a production-code size rule does not reach it.
#                The witness is the reason, from the closed set {registry, test-harness}.
#   multi-axis   exactly two `;`-separated names. The first is the resident side's item,
#                which the file declares as a `fn`, `struct`, `enum`, `trait`, `impl` or
#                `mod`. The second is the other side's process entry point: a subcommand
#                name out of `crates/cogneva/src/cli.rs`'s dispatch table, the one that
#                Job's container runs. The entry point is what makes the claim structural
#                -- it is read off a binary's own command table rather than off a story
#                about a run that once happened. This file is why that distinction is
#                on such a story, and its two sides are two loops in one resident
#                process, with no entry point running either alone.
#   single-axis  exactly one such name: the item that carries the file's one cadence.
#   exempt       exactly one reason token from the closed set above.
# The test recomputes the population and the byte sizes; nothing here is asserted against
# a number that was copied. A file that crosses the threshold needs a row, and a row whose
# file fell below it — or left the tree — has to go.
